title: All surface groupings of eight cells belong to one of thirteen types

fields.label: Label
fields.value: All surface groupings of eight cells belong to one of thirteen types

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because n cells sharing a common outer boundary and meeting three at a time need n − 3 intermediate partitions, every possible grouping of eight cells all reaching the surface belongs to one of thirteen topological types, so all drawings of such eight-celled structures represent one of these types.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: n cells meeting three at a time with a common outer boundary need n - 3 partitions; n = 8 gives 13 types

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: all possible groupings or arrangements whatsoever of eight cells (where all take part in the _surface_ of the group, none being submerged or wholly enveloped by the rest) are referable to some one or other of _thirteen_ types or forms.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Thirteen types of eight-celled groups”. Scope: eight-celled aggregates of plants and animals with all cells at the surface (segmenting eggs, apical cones, discs)

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: n cells meeting three at a time with a common outer boundary need n - 3 partitions; n = 8 gives 13 types

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-09: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The combinatorial component can be checked exactly and observations can test the empirical universality. Existing images cover important cases, but not every plant and animal drawing or all interpretations of the thirteen-type classification.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate admissible planar contact graphs for eight surface-reaching cells under triple-junction constraints, then classify observed eight-cell aggregates and test whether all fit exactly thirteen types.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Observed 3D contacts can be ambiguous near vertices.

The mathematical count depends sensitively on unstated equivalence and admissibility conventions.

fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.76
data existence: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.5
discriminating power: 0.88
operationalizability: 0.92

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The enumeration is largely a theorem about partitions, and datasets test only whether real surface groups obey its premises and look like the listed types. Public cleavage and embryo images support that conformity check for a few organisms. They do not convert the combinatorial statement into an independent empirical law, which limits both discriminating power and scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify surface eight-cell groups, animal and plant, into the thirteen topological types implied by three-way meetings and no submerged cell, and count exceptions. Every group that meets those premises falling into one of the thirteen types would support the empirical rider; a recurring surface arrangement that meets the premises and fits none of the types would refute the enumeration.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
If the three-way and all-cells-on-the-surface premises hold, the thirteen types are a combinatorial list, and images cannot reveal a fourteenth type without breaking a premise.

Many real eight-cell groups include an internal cell or a transient four-way junction and so sit outside the claim's antecedent.
